_note: Simulator settings. Fitted constants (home court, slope) are NOT here: they're fitted on 2025-26 games by `python -m tradesim.fit` and saved to data/model/fit.json.

player_value._replacement_bpm: Basketball-Reference's replacement level (the BPM used for VORP).
player_value._shrink_minutes: BPM is noisy in small samples, so each player's BPM is blended with replacement level as if he'd also played this many replacement-level minutes.

minutes._games_floor: Minutes per game = minutes / max(games, 20), so a player with a few garbage-time games doesn't look like a starter.
minutes._no_stats_mpg: Expected minutes for players with no 2025-26 stats (2026 draft picks by pick number; injured veterans use 'other').

simulation._highlight: A team not in the trade is highlighted if a change is beyond 2 Monte Carlo SE AND at least this big (wins, or points of playoff / play-in / #1-seed odds). Paired changes are so precise that tiny ripple effects would otherwise flag every team.
simulation._chunk_size: Seasons simulated at once. Keeps memory flat (about 150 MB) whatever n_seasons is.

ratings._note: Player-impact model settings. Fitted values (recency weight, shrinkage, age curve, rookie curve, K, SE, residual persistence) are written to data/model/ratings_fit.json by `python -m tradesim.ratings`.
ratings._minutes_prior_games: Minutes per game PLAYED = this season's blended with last season's, as if last season counted for 5 games. Projected minutes per team game = that x expected share of games played.
ratings._availability_prior_games: Games-played share is shrunk toward the league average as if the player had also played this many games at the average rate.

rotation._max_extra_minutes: When teammates are out, a player can take at most this many minutes on top of his usual role.
rotation._diminishing_returns: Simplification, default mild: if the top-3 players add more than `threshold` points (impact x minutes / 48), 15% of the excess is removed.

suggestions._max_asset_reuse: Diversity: an outgoing player or pick may appear in at most this many of a team's suggestions, so the ideas can be combined. null = no limit.
suggestions._max_partner_loss_wins: Realism rule for suggestions only (not the cap checker): skip trades that cost the partner more than this many projected wins. null = pure 'best legal trade by win gain', which produces heists (e.g. a superstar for a role player).
suggestions._min_win_gain: Only suggest trades that add at least this many projected wins.

data._max_unmatched_rows: python -m tradesim.build_data refuses to write league.json if more input rows than this (contracts with no roster match or a different team, no-trade / veto entries naming nobody) fail to join. Two-way players without a standard contract don't count.
data._max_age_days: The app warns when league.json's data (its oldest roster / contract / cap / stats source) is older than this many days.
